questions.q: What does "non-fungible" actually mean, in the context of ERC-721?
options: Each token is unique and used to identify something or someone in a distinct way
Each token is identical and interchangeable, like a dollar bill
The token can never be transferred to another owner
The token has no real value at all
questions.explain: Unlike ERC-20's fungible tokens, every ERC-721 token is unique — that uniqueness is the entire point of the standard.

questions.q: What real state does every ERC-721 token carry that makes it unique?
options: Its own uint256 tokenId
A shared totalSupply value
A fixed price in ETH
A symbol string, just like ERC-20
questions.explain: Every ERC-721 token has its own distinct tokenId — this is the real, defining piece of state that makes each token individually identifiable.

questions.q: Why is an ENS name like `vitalik.eth` a real example of an NFT?
options: Registering the name creates an NFT that the registrant actually owns, instead of just a normal account
ENS names are not actually NFTs at all
ENS names are only usable by Ethereum's core developers
ENS is a completely separate blockchain from Ethereum
questions.explain: ENS uses the NFT standard to represent ownership of a human-readable domain name — registering harris.eth actually mints you an NFT.

questions.q: What real Solidity concepts does ERC-721 rely on, per this lesson?
options: Mappings for ownership, events for transfers, modifiers like onlyOwner, and interfaces
Only loops and no other Solidity feature
A completely different programming language from Solidity
Nothing covered elsewhere in this course
questions.explain: ERC-721 combines the same real Solidity tools covered throughout this chapter — mappings, events, modifiers, and interfaces — nothing new is invented from scratch.

questions.q: What are the two real ways to build an ERC-721 contract, per this lesson?
options: Use an audited library like OpenZeppelin, or build the contract entirely from scratch
Only OpenZeppelin — there's no other valid approach
Only writing from scratch — libraries can't be used for NFTs
Buy a pre-deployed contract from an exchange
questions.explain: Just like with ERC-20, developers can either extend an audited library like OpenZeppelin, or implement every function themselves.
